Guided notes for Lesson 1-1: Prime Factorization  (Standard 6.NS.4)

Content objective: I can write a number as a product of its prime factors using a factor tree.
Language objective: I can explain how I broke a number down using the words prime number, composite number, factor, and exponent.

items.title: 📘 Vocabulary

items.title: A whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors, 1 and itself, is a ___ number.
items.help: Term: Prime number

items.title: A whole number greater than 1 that has more than two factors is a ___ number.
items.help: Term: Composite number

items.title: Prime factorization: ___
items.help: Term: Prime factorization

items.title: I can break a number into its prime factors step by step using a ___.
items.help: Term: Factor tree

items.title: In 2³, the small number 3 is the ___ and it shows 2 is multiplied 3 times.

items.title: 🗣️ Turn & Talk
Mission Control needs to break the 60 supply crates into prime parts. Is 60 a prime number or a composite number, and how can you tell before you even start the factor tree?
Look at your factor tree for 60. How did you decide which numbers to break apart first, and how do you know when to stop?
The party planner has 72 balloons. How could the prime factorization of 72 help her find every way to arrange the balloons in equal rows?
How is a prime number different from a composite number, and why can every composite number be written as a product of primes?

forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 1-1: Prime Factorization (Standard 6.NS.4). 30 questions, 30 points.

items.title: What is the prime factorization of 84?
items.explanation: 84 = 2 × 42 = 2 × 2 × 21 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7. All factors are prime.

items.title: Which number has the prime factorization 2³ × 5?
A number's prime factorization is 2² × 3 × 5. What is the number?
Which list shows ONLY prime numbers?
items.explanation: 2, 3, 11, and 17 each have exactly two factors. The other lists contain composite numbers like 4, 9, or 12.

items.title: Which of the following is a prime number?
items.explanation: 17 has exactly two factors: 1 and 17. 15 = 3 × 5, 21 = 3 × 7, and 9 = 3 × 3, so they are all composite.

items.title: What is the prime factorization of 30?
items.explanation: 30 = 2 × 15 = 2 × 3 × 5. All three factors (2, 3, 5) are prime, so 2 × 3 × 5 is the prime factorization.

items.title: What is the prime factorization of 18?
items.explanation: 18 = 2 × 9 = 2 × 3 × 3. Both 2 and 3 are prime, so 2 × 3 × 3 is the prime factorization.

items.title: Which of these numbers is composite?
items.explanation: 27 = 3 × 9 = 3 × 3 × 3, so it has more than two factors. 23, 29, and 31 are all prime.

items.title: Two students found different factor trees for 60. Student A started with 2 × 30. Student B started with 6 × 10. Which statement is true?
choices: Both get the same prime factorization: 2 × 2 × 3 × 5
Only Student A gets the correct prime factorization
Only Student B gets the correct prime factorization
They will get different prime factorizations
items.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic says every composite number has exactly one prime factorization. No matter how you start the factor tree, you always end with 2 × 2 × 3 × 5.

forms.title: 🚀 1-2 Quiz — Greatest Common Factor
forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 1-2: Greatest Common Factor (Standard 6.NS.4). 28 questions, 28 points.

items.title: What is the GCF of 24 and 36?
items.explanation: 24 = 2³ × 3 and 36 = 2² × 3². The common factors are 2² × 3 = 12.

items.title: What is the GCF of 18 and 30?
items.explanation: 18 = 2 × 3² and 30 = 2 × 3 × 5. Common factors: 2 × 3 = 6.

items.title: A baker has 16 muffins and 24 cookies. She makes identical gift boxes using all the treats. What is the greatest number of boxes?
items.explanation: GCF of 16 and 24 is 8, so she can make 8 equal boxes.

items.title: Which pair of numbers has a GCF of 1?
items.explanation: 8 = 2³ and 15 = 3 × 5 share no common prime factors, so the GCF is 1.

items.title: What is the GCF of 8 and 12?
items.explanation: Factors of 8: 1, 2, 4, 8. Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. The largest common factor is 4.

items.title: Which pair of numbers has a GCF of 5?
items.explanation: 15 = 3 × 5, 25 = 5 × 5. Both share the factor 5, and 5 is the largest shared factor.

items.title: What is the GCF of 14 and 21?
items.explanation: Factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14. Factors of 21: 1, 3, 7, 21. The largest common factor is 7.

items.title: What is the GCF of 9 and 15?
items.explanation: Factors of 9: 1, 3, 9. Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. The largest common factor is 3.

items.title: A teacher has 36 pencils and 48 erasers. She wants to make identical supply bags with no items left over. What is the greatest number of bags she can make?
items.explanation: GCF(36, 48) = 12. She can make 12 bags, each with 3 pencils and 4 erasers.

items.title: Two buses leave the station at 8:00 AM. Bus A returns every 15 minutes and Bus B returns every 20 minutes. When is the next time both buses are at the station together?
items.explanation: LCM(15, 20) = 60 minutes. Both buses return together 60 minutes after 8:00 AM, at 9:00 AM.

items.explanation: You are finding how many 1/4-foot pieces fit into 5 feet, which is 5 ÷ 1/4 = 5 × 4 = 20 books.

forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 3-2: Ratio Tables (Standard 6.RP.3a). 16 questions, 16 points.

items.title: A ratio table shows 3 tickets cost $12. How much do 7 tickets cost?
items.explanation: Each ticket costs $12 ÷ 3 = $4, so 7 tickets cost 7 × $4 = $28.

items.title: In a ratio table, 4 maps to 10. What does 12 map to?
items.explanation: 12 is 3 times 4, so multiply 10 by 3 to get 30.

items.title: A ratio table keeps the ratio 5:8. If one row is 15, what is its partner value?
items.explanation: 15 is 3 times 5, so the partner is 3 times 8 = 24.

items.title: A recipe uses 3 eggs for every 5 cups of flour. How many eggs are needed for 15 cups of flour?
items.explanation: The scale factor is 15 ÷ 5 = 3. Multiply the eggs by 3: 3 × 3 = 9 eggs.

items.title: Which row does NOT belong in a ratio table for 4:5?
items.explanation: 6:10 simplifies to 3:5, not 4:5. The other ratios (8:10, 12:15, 16:20) all simplify to 4:5.

items.title: A ratio table shows 3:7, 6:14, and 9:21. What is the next row?
items.explanation: The pattern adds 3 to the first value and 7 to the second each time. After 9:21: 9+3=12 and 21+7=28. The next row is 12:28.

items.title: A ratio table for 2:5 starts with 2:5, 4:10. What is the third row?
items.explanation: The additive pattern adds 2 to the first value and 5 to the second. 4+2=6 and 10+5=15. The third row is 6:15.

items.title: In a ratio table, the ratio of sugar to butter is 3:2. If you use 12 cups of sugar, how many cups of butter do you need?
items.explanation: Scale factor: 12 ÷ 3 = 4. Multiply butter by 4: 2 × 4 = 8 cups of butter.

items.title: A ratio table shows 5:8, 10:16, 15:24. What scale factor was used from the first row to the third row?
items.explanation: From 5 to 15: 15 ÷ 5 = 3. From 8 to 24: 24 ÷ 8 = 3. The scale factor is 3.

forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 3-3: Graph Ratio Tables (Standard 6.RP.3a). 11 questions, 11 points.

items.title: A graph of a ratio passes through (0,0) and (2,6). What point also lies on the line?
items.explanation: The ratio is 6 to 2 = 3 to 1, so (4, 12) follows the same pattern.

items.title: On a ratio graph each apple costs $2. Which point shows 5 apples?
items.explanation: 5 apples at $2 each is $10, so the point is (5, 10).

items.title: A line through the origin contains (3, 9). What is the unit rate (y per 1 x)?
items.explanation: 9 ÷ 3 = 3, so y increases by 3 for each 1 unit of x.

items.title: Why do graphs of equivalent ratios start at the origin (0,0)?
choices: Because 0 of one quantity pairs with 0 of the other
Because every line starts at zero
items.explanation: When you have 0 of one amount you have 0 of the other, so the line passes through (0,0).

items.title: A ratio table shows (2, 6), (4, 12), and (6, 18). Which ordered pair comes next if the pattern continues?
items.explanation: The pattern adds 2 to x and 6 to y each time. After (6, 18): x = 6+2 = 8, y = 18+6 = 24. The next point is (8, 24).

items.title: When you graph equivalent ratios, the points will always form what shape?
choices: A straight line through the origin
items.explanation: Equivalent ratios are proportional, so their graph is always a straight line that passes through the origin (0, 0).

items.title: A ratio table shows (2, 8), (3, 12), and (5, 20). What is the y-value when x = 7?
items.explanation: The ratio is y/x = 8/2 = 4. For every x, y = 4x. When x = 7: y = 4 × 7 = 28.

items.title: Which point would NOT be on the graph of the ratio 1:5?
items.explanation: For the ratio 1:5, every y-value should be 5 times the x-value. (3, 10): 5 × 3 = 15, not 10. So (3, 10) does not belong.

items.title: Points from a ratio table are plotted at (1, 4), (2, 8), and (3, 12). What is the ratio of y to x for each point?
items.explanation: For each point: 4÷1 = 4, 8÷2 = 4, 12÷3 = 4. The ratio of y to x is always 4:1.

items.title: Two students graph ratio tables. Student A plots (1,2), (2,4), (3,6). Student B plots (1,3), (2,6), (3,9). Whose line is steeper?
items.explanation: Student A's ratio is 1:2 (y goes up 2 for each 1 in x). Student B's ratio is 1:3 (y goes up 3 for each 1 in x). A higher rate of change means a steeper line, so Student B's is steeper.

items.title: Exit Ticket: A ratio table shows cups of rice to cups of water: (1, 2), (2, 4), (3, 6). If you plot these points, the line passes through which point?
items.explanation: The ratio is 1:2, so for 5 cups of rice you need 5 × 2 = 10 cups of water. The point (5, 10) continues the pattern.

items.title: A recipe for 4 people uses 6 eggs. How many eggs for 10 people?
items.explanation: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 eggs per person; 1.5 × 10 = 15 eggs.

items.title: A runner covers 12 km in 4 hours. How long to cover 21 km at the same speed?
items.explanation: Speed is 3 km/h; 21 ÷ 3 = 7 hours.

items.title: 5 notebooks cost $7.50. What is the cost of 12 notebooks?
A bakery makes 24 cookies in 3 batches. What is the unit rate of cookies per batch?
items.explanation: Unit rate: 24 cookies ÷ 3 batches = 8 cookies per batch.

items.title: Apples cost $5 for 4 pounds. What is the cost per pound?
items.explanation: Unit rate: $5 ÷ 4 pounds = $1.25 per pound.

items.title: A cyclist rides 36 miles in 3 hours. At the same rate, how far will she ride in 5 hours?
items.explanation: Unit rate: 36 ÷ 3 = 12 miles per hour. In 5 hours: 12 × 5 = 60 miles.

items.title: A printer prints 45 pages in 9 minutes. How many pages does it print per minute?
items.explanation: Unit rate: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 pages per minute.

items.title: A car travels 150 miles in 3 hours. A bus travels 200 miles in 5 hours. Which vehicle is faster?
items.explanation: Car: 150÷3 = 50 mph. Bus: 200÷5 = 40 mph. The car travels faster at 50 mph vs. 40 mph.

items.explanation: Unit rate: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 pages per minute. In 12 minutes: 6 × 12 = 72 pages.

forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 5-1: Area of Parallelograms (Standard 6.G.1). 21 questions, 21 points.

items.title: A parallelogram has base 9 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?
items.explanation: Area = base × height = 9 × 6 = 54 cm².

items.title: A parallelogram has area 48 m² and base 8 m. What is its height?
items.explanation: height = area ÷ base = 48 ÷ 8 = 6 m.

items.title: Why is a parallelogram's area base × height and not base × slant side?
choices: Height is the perpendicular distance between the bases
The slant side is always longer
The base is always the longest side
items.explanation: Area uses the perpendicular height, not the slanted side length.

items.title: A parallelogram has base 12 in and height 4.5 in. What is its area?
What is the area of a parallelogram with base 10 cm and height 7 cm?
items.explanation: A = b × h = 10 × 7 = 70 square centimeters.

items.title: A parallelogram has an area of 54 sq ft and a base of 9 ft. What is the height?
What is the area of a parallelogram with base 9 cm and height 5 cm?
items.explanation: A = b × h = 9 × 5 = 45 square centimeters.

items.title: Which measurement is the height of a parallelogram?
choices: The perpendicular distance between the base and the opposite side
The length of the slanted side
items.explanation: The height is always the perpendicular (straight up-and-down) distance between the base and the opposite side, not the slanted side.

items.title: A taxi charges $3 plus $2 per mile. The ride cost $15. Which equation finds the miles m?

items.title: Solve: 4x = 28. How many items if each is $4 and total is $28?
items.explanation: 28 ÷ 4 = 7 items.

items.title: You have $50 and spend $8 per ticket. Which inequality shows how many tickets t you can buy?
items.explanation: Total spent must be 50 or less: 8t ≤ 50 (so t ≤ 6 whole tickets).

items.title: Solve: x − 12 = 20.
items.explanation: Add 12 to both sides: x = 32.

items.title: A museum has some paintings. After adding 12, they have 45. Which equation models this?
items.explanation: 'Adding 12' to the original number gives 45: p + 12 = 45. Solve: p = 33.

items.title: A detective needs more than 8 hours to finish the investigation. She has already worked 3 hours. Which inequality represents the additional hours h she needs?
items.explanation: 3 hours plus additional hours h must be more than 8: 3 + h > 8. Solve: h > 5.

items.title: Which model is correct for: 'A number divided by 6 equals 7'?
items.explanation: Divided by 6 is n / 6. Equals 7 means = 7. So n / 6 = 7.

items.title: A bus can carry at most 48 passengers. There are already 31 on board. Which inequality shows how many more can board?
items.explanation: 'At most 48' means the total must be ≤ 48. So 31 + p ≤ 48. Solve: p ≤ 17.

items.title: A student solved 4n = 52 and got n = 13. Is the answer reasonable if n represents the number of notebooks in a box?
choices: Yes — 13 notebooks per box is reasonable
Yes — but only if n is a fraction
items.explanation: 4 × 13 = 52 ✓. 13 notebooks per box is a reasonable whole number answer.

forms.title: 🏀 8-3 Quiz — Mean Absolute Deviation
forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 8-3: Mean Absolute Deviation (Standard 6.SP.5c). 14 questions, 14 points.

items.title: The data 5, 7, 9 has mean 7. What is the mean absolute deviation (MAD)?
items.explanation: Distances from 7 are 2, 0, 2; mean = 4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.33.

items.title: What does a larger MAD tell you about a data set?
choices: The values are more spread out from the mean
items.explanation: MAD measures average distance from the mean; larger MAD means more spread.

items.title: The data 10, 10, 10, 10 has what MAD?
items.explanation: Every value equals the mean, so each distance is 0 and MAD = 0.

items.title: For the data 2, 4, 6 (mean 4), what is the MAD?
items.explanation: Distances are 2, 0, 2; mean = 4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.33.

items.title: The mean of a data set is 15. One value is 11. What is the absolute deviation of that value from the mean?
items.explanation: Deviation = 11 − 15 = −4. Absolute deviation = |−4| = 4.

items.title: A data set has absolute deviations of 3, 1, 5, 2, 4. What is the MAD?
items.explanation: Sum of absolute deviations = 3 + 1 + 5 + 2 + 4 = 15. MAD = 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

items.title: The mean of a data set is 20. A value is 26. What is the absolute deviation?
items.explanation: Deviation = 26 − 20 = 6. Absolute deviation = |6| = 6.

items.title: Team A has MAD = 2.1 points. Team B has MAD = 6.8 points. Which team is more consistent?
choices: Team A — lower MAD means scores are closer to the mean
Team B — higher MAD means better performance
items.explanation: Lower MAD means less spread — Team A's scores stay closer to their average, making them more consistent.

items.title: Two runners have the same average time of 60 seconds. Runner A's MAD is 1.2 seconds. Runner B's MAD is 5.8 seconds. Which runner is the coach more likely to pick for a relay race that needs a reliable time?
choices: Runner A — lower MAD means more consistent times
Runner B — higher MAD means faster potential
Either — they have the same average
Neither — MAD doesn't matter for relay races
items.explanation: Runner A's MAD of 1.2 means times are usually within 1.2 seconds of 60. Runner B's times vary more widely. For reliability, pick Runner A.

items.explanation: The data is symmetric with no outliers, so the mean (8.7) best represents the typical score.

items.title: A runner's mile times are: 7:10, 7:15, 7:12, 7:20, 12:00. The 12:00 was due to a cramp. Which measure best represents a typical mile?
choices: Median — the outlier 12:00 pulls the mean too high
Mean — it uses all the data
Mode — it shows the most common time
items.explanation: The 12:00 is an outlier that pulls the mean up. The median (7:15) better represents the runner's typical time.

items.title: Data set: 5, 6, 7, 7, 8, 50. The mean is about 13.8 and the median is 7. Which better represents the typical value?
choices: Median (7) — the outlier 50 inflates the mean
items.explanation: The mean (13.8) is higher than 5 of the 6 values because the outlier 50 pulls it up. The median (7) better represents a typical value.

items.title: A baseball player's batting averages over 6 seasons are: .280, .295, .290, .285, .300, .110. The .110 was an injury-shortened season. Which measure better represents the player's typical batting average?
choices: Median, because the .110 outlier pulls the mean down
Mean, because it uses all the data
Mean, because .110 is a real season
items.explanation: The .110 is an outlier that pulls the mean down to .260. The median (.2875) better represents typical performance because it isn't affected by the extreme value.

items.title: A histogram differs from a bar graph because...

items.title: A histogram bin for 10–19 has a bar height of 6. What does 6 represent?
choices: 6 data values fall in that interval
items.explanation: The bar height is the frequency — how many values fall in that bin.

items.explanation: 4 + 9 + 2 = 15 data values.

items.title: Why should histogram intervals be equal in width?
choices: So the bars fairly compare how many values fall in each range
items.explanation: Equal widths make frequency comparisons fair across bins.

items.title: A histogram shows these frequencies: 0–4: 3 players, 5–9: 8 players, 10–14: 12 players, 15–19: 5 players. How many players are represented in total?
items.explanation: Add all frequencies: 3 + 8 + 12 + 5 = 28 players.

items.title: In a histogram, what does the height of each bar represent?
choices: The frequency (count) of data in that interval
The average of the data in that interval
items.explanation: Each bar's height shows the frequency — how many data values fall within that interval.

items.title: How is a histogram different from a regular bar graph?
choices: Histogram bars touch (no gaps) because the intervals are continuous ranges
Histograms use colors and bar graphs don't
Bar graphs show numbers and histograms show words
items.explanation: In a histogram, bars touch because each interval connects to the next (0–9, 10–19, etc.) — the data is continuous.

items.title: A histogram has intervals: 0–4, 5–9, 10–14, 15–19. What is the width of each interval?
items.explanation: Each interval covers 5 values (0,1,2,3,4 then 5,6,7,8,9 etc.), so the width is 5.

choices: The mean is much higher than the median

items.explanation: In a symmetric distribution, the mean and median are approximately equal because the data is balanced on both sides.

items.title: Which word describes the direction of the TAIL, not the peak?
choices: Skew — the direction of the long tail tells you the skew direction
Skew — the direction of the peak tells you the skew direction
Skew — the direction the median points
Skew — the direction of the mode
items.explanation: The skew direction is named after the TAIL. If the tail stretches to the right, it is skewed right, even though the peak is on the left.

items.title: A dot plot of goals scored per game shows: 0(5 dots), 1(7 dots), 2(4 dots), 3(2 dots), 4(1 dot). What is the shape?
choices: Skewed right — most values at the low end with a tail to the right
Skewed left — most values at the high end
Uniform — all bars the same height
items.explanation: The data peaks at 0–1 goals and tails off toward 4. Most data is on the left with fewer values stretching right — this is skewed right.

items.explanation: The data clusters on the left (40–60) with a tail to the right (90–100). This is skewed right. The median is best because the mean would be pulled toward the high values.

items.title: Where is -3/4 located on the number line?

items.title: Which rational number is closest to 0 on the number line?
items.explanation: |-1/4| = 0.25, |0.5| = 0.5, |-2| = 2, |1.75| = 1.75. Since 0.25 is the smallest absolute value, -1/4 is closest to zero.

forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 9-6: Distance on the Coordinate Plane (Standard 6.NS.8). 9 questions, 9 points.

items.title: What is the distance between (2, 3) and (2, 9)?
items.explanation: Same x, so subtract y-values: 9 − 3 = 6 units.

items.title: What is the distance between (-4, 1) and (5, 1)?
items.explanation: Same y; distance = |5 − (-4)| = 9 units.

items.title: A point is at (-3, 2) and another at (-3, -5). How far apart are they?
items.explanation: Same x; distance = |2 − (-5)| = 7 units.

items.title: Why can you find the distance between (1, 4) and (6, 4) by subtracting x-values?
choices: They have the same y-coordinate, so the segment is horizontal
Distance is always the larger number
You must always add the coordinates
items.explanation: Equal y-values mean a horizontal segment, so distance = |6 − 1| = 5.

items.title: What is the distance between (-4, 3) and (2, 3)?
items.explanation: Both points have y = 3, so this is a horizontal distance. |2 - (-4)| = |2 + 4| = 6 units.

items.title: What is the distance between (5, -2) and (5, 4)?
items.explanation: Both points have x = 5, so this is a vertical distance. |4 - (-2)| = |4 + 2| = 6 units.

items.title: A rectangle has vertices at (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4), (1, 4). What is its perimeter?
items.explanation: Width = 5 - 1 = 4. Height = 4 - 1 = 3. Perimeter = 2(4 + 3) = 14.

items.title: Two points are at (-3, -7) and (-3, 5). What is the distance between them?
items.explanation: Same x = -3. Distance = |5 - (-7)| = |5 + 7| = 12 units.

items.title: Exit Ticket: What is the distance between the points (3, -2) and (3, 5)?
items.explanation: Both points share x = 3, so this is a vertical distance. |5 - (-2)| = |5 + 2| = 7 units.

forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 10-1: Volume with Whole Number Edges (Standard 6.G.2). 9 questions, 9 points.

items.title: A box is 4 units long, 3 wide, and 2 tall. What is its volume?
items.explanation: V = l × w × h = 4 × 3 × 2 = 24 cubic units.

items.title: How many unit cubes fill a box that is 5 by 2 by 3?
items.explanation: 5 × 2 × 3 = 30 unit cubes.

items.title: A cube has edges of 4 units. What is its volume?
items.explanation: V = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64 cubic units.

items.title: A box has volume 36 cubic units. Its base is 6 by 2. What is its height?
items.explanation: Base area = 12; height = 36 ÷ 12 = 3 units.

items.title: What is the volume of a rectangular prism with l = 7 in, w = 3 in, h = 4 in?
items.explanation: V = l × w × h = 7 × 3 × 4 = 84 cubic inches.

items.title: A time capsule box has a volume of 120 cm³. Its length is 10 cm and width is 4 cm. What is its height?
Which unit is used for volume?
items.explanation: Volume measures 3D space, so it uses cubic units like in³. Square units (in²) are for area, and inches are for length.

items.title: Two storage bins: Bin A is 8 × 6 × 5 inches. Bin B is 9 × 4 × 7 inches. Which holds more and by how much?
items.explanation: Bin A: 8 × 6 × 5 = 240 in³. Bin B: 9 × 4 × 7 = 252 in³. Bin B holds 12 in³ more.

items.title: Exit Ticket: A rectangular prism has l = 11 in, w = 5 in, h = 4 in. What is the volume?
items.explanation: V = 11 × 5 × 4 = 220 cubic inches. Remember: volume uses cubic units (in³).

items.explanation: A cube has 6 identical faces. Each face: 5 × 5 = 25 cm². Total SA = 6 × 25 = 150 cm².

forms.title: 📦 10-4 Quiz — Surface Area of Prisms
forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 10-4: Surface Area of Prisms (Standard 6.G.4). 15 questions, 15 points.

items.title: A rectangular prism is 5 by 3 by 2. What is its surface area?
A cube has surface area 96 cm². What is the area of one face?
items.explanation: A cube has 6 equal faces: 96 ÷ 6 = 16 cm² per face.

items.title: To wrap a gift box 4 by 4 by 4 cm, how much paper covers the surface (no overlap)?
items.explanation: Each face is 16; 6 × 16 = 96 cm².

items.title: A prism is 10 by 2 by 3. What is its surface area?
What is the surface area of a rectangular prism with l = 5 cm, w = 4 cm, h = 3 cm?
How many faces does a triangular prism have?
items.explanation: A triangular prism has 5 faces: 2 triangular bases and 3 rectangular lateral faces.

items.title: A triangular prism has two triangular bases each with area 12 cm² and three rectangular faces with areas 30 cm², 40 cm², and 40 cm². What is the total surface area?
A triangular prism has triangular bases with base 6 in and height 4 in. The prism is 10 in long and the two slant sides of the triangle are each 5 in. What is the surface area?
items.explanation: Triangular bases: 2 × (½ × 6 × 4) = 24 in². Three rectangular faces: 6(10) + 5(10) + 5(10) = 60 + 50 + 50 = 160 in². SA = 24 + 160 = 184 in².

Guided notes for Lesson 10-5: Surface Area of Pyramids  (Standard 6.G.4)

Language objective: I can explain my work using the words pyramid, slant height, lateral face, and base.

forms.title: 📦 10-5 Quiz — Surface Area of Pyramids
forms.description: Autograded quiz for Lesson 10-5: Surface Area of Pyramids (Standard 6.G.4). 9 questions, 9 points.

items.title: A square pyramid has a base that is 4 by 4 and 4 triangular faces each 10 sq units. What is the surface area?
items.explanation: Base 4 × 4 = 16, plus 4 triangles × 10 = 40; total = 56 sq units.

items.title: How many triangular faces does a square pyramid have?
items.explanation: A square pyramid has 4 triangular faces meeting at the top, plus 1 square base.

items.title: A triangular pyramid (all faces triangles) has 4 faces each with area 9 cm². What is the surface area?
items.explanation: 4 faces × 9 = 36 cm².

items.title: To find a pyramid's surface area, you...
choices: Add the base area to the areas of all the triangular faces
Multiply length by width by height
Subtract the triangles from the base
items.explanation: Surface area = base area + the areas of all the side (triangular) faces.

items.title: A square pyramid has a base edge of 5 in and a slant height of 7 in. What is the surface area?
items.explanation: Base: 5 × 5 = 25 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 5 × 7 = 17.5 in². Four faces: 4 × 17.5 = 70 in². SA = 25 + 70 = 95 in².

items.title: How many lateral (triangular) faces does a square pyramid have?
items.explanation: A square pyramid has a square base and 4 triangular lateral faces — one for each side of the square.

items.title: What is the area of one triangular face with base 8 in and slant height 6 in?
items.explanation: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 8 × 6 = 24 in².

items.title: A square pyramid has a base area of 49 cm² and a total lateral area of 84 cm². What is the surface area?
items.explanation: SA = Base Area + Lateral Area = 49 + 84 = 133 cm².

items.title: Exit Ticket: A square pyramid has a base edge of 6 in and a slant height of 5 in. What is the total surface area?
items.explanation: Base: 6 × 6 = 36 in². Each lateral face: ½ × 6 × 5 = 15 in². Four faces: 4 × 15 = 60 in². SA = 36 + 60 = 96 in². Surface area uses square units (in²).
